title: Inclusive Limit Ambiguity (`stop` vs `last`)
pattern: A function or struct defining an inclusive upper limit named `stop` or `end` alongside `start` or `begin`.
why_bad: The word `stop` is semantically ambiguous; it does not clearly convey whether the boundary is inclusive or exclusive, leading to classic off-by-one errors (fencepost errors) when developers assume the opposite behavior.
detection: Match parameters or fields named `stop` used in inclusive contexts (like `..=` in Rust) or where the name fails to denote inclusion.
source: *The Art of Readable Code* by Dustin Boswell and Trevor Foucher (Chapter 3, p. 26).
